body:
Aloha from Hawaii!  Well, not really, I’m actualy from Seattle, but with this cold weather, I wish it were Hawaii.  I’m here today to tell a little tale about a trip I took to Phoenix.



I found out that I was going to be able to go to Phoenix a whole 8 days before the tourny was to be played, thus sneaking in just in time for cheap airline tickets.  So, I fly into Phoenix Friday night, and am picked up at the airport by my good friend George, and he drops me off at my grandparents house.  I then call Chris Shaner, and ask if he can still give me a ride down to Tempe.  Chris says, "Yeah, if you want to ride with Roach."  I’m like "that’s cool."



Okay, so it’s now 2:00 in the morning, and I look at my decks.  My Lightside is my hidden base operative deck, that I’ve been tweeking for the last 2 weeks, and it’s set.  For DS, I have "Harvilla Huntdown", "Sagan TIE’s" and "Hawkins Branus" built.  I decide on Hunt, as it’s the most solid I have, and it is just a good deck.



So it’s now 3:00, and I go to sleep:



6:45 A.M.:

I wake up, get a bite to eat, get dressed, brush teeth, then I throw up!  WTF is up with that.  so I brush my teath again, drink water to settle the stomach, and scarf down more food... I see Chris pull up, so out the door I go, hugging my grandma goodbye, and am on my way to Tempe.



We roll into the card shop, and I’m just exstatic at all the faces I get to see.  Alot of people I used to play against, a few others that happend to be in town, and then others along the lines of Clint, Steve, Brian, Kyle, etc.  Awsome.



So, I’m there, making some trades, talking smack with Girard and others, and we start about 10, an hour late (note to Girard:  Any tourny that starts before noon is considered on time to me).  So pairing are getting called out, and I here my name announced, against some other guy named Clint Hays.  Hmm, this should prove to be entertaining.



Game 1:  DS vs. Clint Hays’ Agents Speeders

Well, were do I begin?  I shall first say that I have never once played against a speeder deck, so I have no idea really what is coming.  I understand the beatdown, can visulize the beatdown, but for some reason, the data just does not compute.  I play the waiting game this game, and realize that was the mistake.  I gave Clint way to much time to set his hand up, and let him deploy two Manuevering Flaps (it’s not unique, check it out) which detroys my chance at Alter.  so, I make a move, deploy Vader/Tarkin, and pick up some... well, I got hit for 40 power to my 10.  Wow.  (note, I verified his deck, and there were only 7 speeders there, apperently the other 8 or so were in his hand)  So, that spanking hurt, but I took it.  After that, the game was pretty uneventful, and I lost by 16.  But hey, I didn’t know how to play against Speeders.

FL 0 (-16)



Game 2: LS vs. John Baril Hoth clouds deck.

Well ,John was slow getting moving, and my deck played out just perfect, setting up Operative drains on some planets, and controlling space and killing his bonuses with menace fades and cancellation.  He complains a bit that he never got his clouds going, and I just smile and nod while staring at the X-wing cannon in hand and starfighter to use them on.  Win by 8

2 (-8)



Game 3: LS vs. Wyatt Evertt Endor speeder mike drains

He get’s a great quick jump, and I lose a few force, but I get my operatives and space going, menace fades to kill his drains and get the huge operative/Space drain going.  He spreads on Endor, but Jedi Luke pays avisist.  FW by 15

4 (+7)



Game 4: DS vs. Joel Massie LS.

Holy Crap, I can’t remember this game!.  I won, but I can’t remember what he played!  FW by 11

6 (+18)



Game 5: DS vs. Matt Rader throne room

This was a difficult came to play, and since I figured he had no BG’s, I deploy my DS docking bay only, to force the issue there.  Well, with the power at the deatstar, and Sarki and Mara at the Throne room, I won the grueling contest.  Game ended with a 4 turn standoff of Vader Tarkin vs. Jedi Luke and EPP Han.  Carida Drain win it. I won by 11

8 (+29)



Game 6:  LS Vs. Shane Watner DS TIE’s

He Starts Throne room, and mob points.  oh, a TIE deck, fun.  I know I have to play my deck, not against his, so I follow this simple plan.  *Get systems out, get operatives in speeders to such systems, have space power, kill his bonuses, and cancel some drains if needed*  Average win by about 8.  Well, I won this game by 5...  most likely my deck was mostly on table  good game nonetheless

10 (+34)



Game 7:  LS vs. Steven Lewis Huntdown

Well well, I get to play Clint and Steve.  That is too cool, I know now that my ticket was worth it to come down.  Well, I trans Term Steve turn 1, but he’s got a holonet trans for me, darn.  Well, I’m slow getting stuff in my hand, and over the course of 2 turns, I lose Kiffex, and 3 operatives from my deck... darn, there goes my major damage.  I can’t stop the visage, and I’ve lost the major damage inflictors I have.  but I can still win... the key card you ask?  Boussh.  I get boussh out, and she lives a turn, but the next, Steve plays Sniper.  It goes through.  Darn.  Now to tell you the bad part.  theres this card call "it’s a trap".  I play two of them.  It cancels Sniper.  I had one in my hand.  oh well.  That causes me to flip, which engages security precautions.  which in turn make me lose alot of force. I played dumb, I coulda won it out, but instead, I lost the noble fight by 11

10 (+23)



Game 8:  Ds vs. Steven Lewis Speeders

WTF?  I have to play Steve?  wow, DS really dominated that earlier round.  so I show hunt, he shows speeders.  Well, I decidee to take a new approach this game.  I have a vader in my hand, and I drop him to tatooine, ignoring my own DB’s, cause I’m not giving him anywhere to run.  so Vader is soon backued up, and then I get Sarkli, Emperor and Janus to the hoth Warrroom.  My Strategy?  Jump on the speeders sites so fast and furious, and cause as much force loss as possible.  I found out that it works...  I end up winning by 13, causing a total of 8 in drains and Visage in the end game...  to his 3... not enough, great game, I beat Steve.  Win by 13

12 (+35)



Okay, so I go 6-2, my two losses being to Clint and Steve, I can’t complain about that at all.  I come in 10th, last of the 6-2’s



Props:

Girard for running a great event

Clint Hays, for signing my speeder for Matt

Steve Lewis, great sportsman

Kyle Craft, The sabbac Master

Mike Mueller, good to see you

DJ, you still suck

Roach, You beat Brian Hunter

Brian Hunter, you kicked some tail

Kevin Shannon, you kicked tail too.

Everyone I saw in Phoenix, good to see you!

The two Jens.  I’d play YJ if I lived there still

And more that I’m forgetting



Slops:

Tim Guzman , The SWRPG shirts look gay

Brandon allen, cause he thinks he’s good

DJ, cause he gave me a ride home

wait, that’s a prop!

Slops, everyone has slops!



Biggest slop



Kyle Craft piece of @#$% that didn’t flush.  You suck!



Everyone in Phoenix, I had a great time, and it was terrific playing you all and meeting even more of you!



Take care

summary: Charles Hickey of Seattle finished 10th, last of the 6–2 players, at the Saturday Mega Tournament of the 2000 Phoenix Mega Weekend with a Hidden Base operative deck and a Hunt Down deck, going 6–2 (12 (+35)) with losses to Clint Hays and Steven Lewis.
notes: Event identification: Hickey flies in Friday night and plays 'the tourny' the next morning (eight games) at a card shop in Tempe, so this is the Saturday 4 November Mega Tournament, not the Sunday Grand Slam. Same hub name as Brian Hunter's d1433 and Steve Marshall's d1419. Parent [[2000 Mega Weekend]].

Cross-check: Clint Hays's report (d1464) game 1 is LS speeders vs 'charles hickey hdadtj', FW by 16, matching Hickey's game 1 loss by 16. Hunter (d1433) records Clint Hays and Steven Lewis at 6–2 in the Swiss.

Light deck linked to [[2000 Phoenix Grand Slam Charles Hickey Hidden Operatives]]: that list says 'Went 3-1 at Phoenix Mega Tourny ... one loss to Steven Lewis by 11, in game 7 (3-0 before that point)', which is this report's Light record exactly. The deck page and [[2000 Phoenix Grand Slam]] file it under the Grand Slam; see discrepancies.

Dark deck: 'I decide on Hunt' from the three Dark decks he built ('Harvilla Huntdown', 'Sagan TIE's', 'Hawkins Branus'); linked to the original Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi (Hays also calls it 'hdadtj'). Hays's 'Agents Speeders' linked to Agents In The Court; Steven Lewis's 'Huntdown' to Hunt Down. Throne Room, TIEs, Hoth clouds and Endor speeders not linked.
Sides from the report's game headers (DS/LS). Game 1 'FL 0 (-16)': full loss.

Names: John Baril, Joel Massie, Shane Watner, Steven Lewis ('Steve Lewis' in the props), Clint Hays link to existing pages (small-world rule). 'Wyatt Evertt' and 'Matt Rader' have no pages; Brian Garrison's d1215 has a 'Wyatt Everet' (Tucson/Phoenix, September 2000), probably the same person: the two spellings should share one page (correct spelling unknown, possibly Everett).
Finish '10th, last of the 6-2's' as stated; player count not given.
Props mention Roach beating Brian Hunter; Roach is a nickname only, not recorded.

discrepancies.text: Charles Hickey's 'Hidden Operatives' list (3–1, one loss to Steven Lewis in game 7) is filed on this hub, but his own report puts that 3–1 Light run in the Saturday 4 November Mega Tournament, where he went 6–2 and finished 10th; he does not mention playing the Grand Slam on Sunday.
